quanteda methods for parsed texts

Source: R/quanteda-methods.R
quanteda-methods.Rd

Methods of quanteda's functions for the output of spacy_parse(): its tokens as a quanteda tokens object, and its documents and their sizes. They need the quanteda package, and are available when both packages are loaded.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'spacyr_parsed'
as.tokens(
  x,
  concatenator = "/",
  include_pos = c("none", "pos", "tag"),
  use_lemma = FALSE,
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'spacyr_parsed'
docnames(x)

# S3 method for class 'spacyr_parsed'
ndoc(x)

# S3 method for class 'spacyr_parsed'
ntoken(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'spacyr_parsed'
ntype(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'spacyr_parsed'
nsentence(x)

Arguments

x

the output of spacy_parse(), or of entity_consolidate() or nounphrase_consolidate()

concatenator

the character that joins a token and its part of speech, when include_pos is not "none"

include_pos

which part of speech to add to each token, after concatenator: "none", the default, for none; "pos" for the column pos; or "tag" for the column tag

use_lemma

if TRUE, the tokens are the lemmas and not the tokens as they are in the text

...

not used

Value

  • as.tokens() returns a quanteda tokens object with the tokens of each document, with the document variables of the corpus that was parsed, if it was a corpus.

  • docnames() returns the names of the documents, and ndoc() their number.

  • ntoken(), ntype() and nsentence() return the number of tokens, of different tokens and of sentences in each document, as an integer vector named by document, in the order of docnames().

Details

The tokens are spaCy's, with its tokens of whitespace, so their positions are those that spacy_match(), spacy_extract_entity() and spacy_extract_nounphrases() report in start_id: see as_index().

Which documents there are

All six methods agree on the documents of x. spacy_parse() keeps with its output the names of all the documents it was given, in their order, and the document variables of a quanteda corpus. So a document in which spaCy found no tokens, such as an empty text, is a document with no tokens here, although it has no row in x.

Taking rows out of x can leave that record as it was. It is therefore used only as far as the rows agree with it:

  • When every document that had tokens still has rows, the documents are all those that were parsed. Removing some of the tokens, such as the punctuation, does not remove a document.

  • When a document that had tokens has no rows left, documents were taken out of x, and the documents are those that have rows. One without tokens is then not kept either.

  • When x has rows that were not parsed with the others, or has no record, as an object saved by an earlier version of spacyr or one that another function made into a new data.frame, the documents are those that have rows, without document variables.

rbind() of parses combines their records when no two of them have a document of the same name: the result has the documents of all of them, and their document variables when all have the same ones. When two parses have a document of the same name, the result has no record, since the rows of the two cannot be told apart: its documents are those that have rows, without document variables. Other ways of combining parses, such as dplyr::bind_rows(), can keep the record of the first. It is then not used when a document has more rows than it had tokens, or a name that the record does not have; give the documents different names to be sure.

The documents are in the order in which they were parsed, or in the order of the rows of x when that is another, with the documents without tokens last.

Earlier versions

Until spacyr 2.0 these methods were part of quanteda. To use them on an object that was saved to a file, load spacyr as well as quanteda, for instance with library("spacyr"): reading the object does not load it.

See also

spacy_parse(), as_index(), quanteda::as.tokens(), quanteda::docnames(), quanteda::ntoken()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
spacy_initialize()
corp <- quanteda::corpus(c(d1 = "And now for something different.",
                           d2 = "",
                           d3 = "Jack and Jill are children."),
                         docvars = data.frame(year = 2001:2003))
parsed <- spacy_parse(corp)

quanteda::docnames(parsed)
quanteda::ntoken(parsed)
quanteda::nsentence(parsed)

toks <- quanteda::as.tokens(parsed)
toks
quanteda::docvars(toks)
quanteda::as.tokens(parsed, include_pos = "pos")
spacy_finalize()
} # }
